subject: Deployment-mode runbook request + POC timeline (Healthlytics)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Deployment-mode runbook request + POC timeline (Healthlytics)

Hi Alicia + Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move toward a trial kickoff: 

1) What we heard (please correct if I misstate):
- Primary constraint: data residency and PHI handling for certain inference flows — you prefer data stay inside your cloud account where possible.
- Traffic profile: intermittent bursts tied to nightly batch jobs and steady low-volume interactive traffic from clinicians.
- Success criteria: latency under 150ms (95th pct) for interactive flows, batch throughput of ~250k tokens/hour, and zero production data sent to third-party storage.

2) Deployment modes we recommended (summary):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding and simplest integration, but would require secure proxying or tokenization to avoid sending raw PHI off your environment.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in our infra with customer tenancy and predictable throughput; good middle ground if you want isolation but not full VPC.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full control and encryption keys in your KMS, recommended if audit + residency are non-negotiable.

3) Ask from you before we draft the trial runbook:
- Confirm which mode you want us to prioritize for the PoC (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC).
- Confirm tech contacts: please add the IT/security lead who will own firewall/KMS/network decisions.
- Any regulatory docs you want included in the trial (SOC2/attestations).

4) Proposed PoC timeline (flexible):
- Week 0: Kickoff + environment access and security Q&A (3–5 business days)
- Week 1–2: Integration of a sample inference flow + telemetry (latency, error rates)
- Week 3: Scale test (batch run) + evaluation against success criteria
- Week 4: Final review, handoff notes, and next-steps for production migration

I attached a trial-charter-template.xlsx and our security-qa.pdf to make it easy to capture owners and artifacts. Marcus (cc'd) and Priya (cc'd) will own the trial orchestration and integration support from Redwood.

Next steps: Alicia/Tom — can you confirm the preferred deployment mode and add Michael Chan (IT) to this thread? If Dedicated or Private, call out any firewall/VPC peering windows you prefer.

Thanks,
Jasmine
--
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A few notes: 

- We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity as the starting point. Reason: predictable throughput for our batch jobs and less operational overhead than a full Private VPC while still keeping data segregation.
- Michael Chan (IT) is our network/security lead — adding him now: michael.chan@healthlytics.com. He will need the SOC2 and any encryption/KMS docs; I attached our initial security questionnaire (we'll fill it out and return).
- Timeline: if we can start kickoff the week of Nov 8, that works for our internal schedule. We'll need Redwood to confirm expected AWS account access for peering (if needed) and a short list of ports/protocols.

Tom and I will prioritize the success criteria list you captured; preliminary note — batch throughput may need to target 300k tokens/hour when we include peak nightly windows. We'll confirm by Friday.

Alicia

Quick clarifying questions from the infra side — Alicia/Michael: 
1) Expected concurrent interactive sessions (clinician-facing) at peak? Knowing concurrent users helps us size dedicated GPU pool and choose model shard/quantization.
2) For batch flows, are transforms happening client-side or will you send raw text to Redwood endpoints? If it's raw, we'll need an agreed masking/tokenization plan.
3) Any preference for the host region (us-west-2 vs us-east-1) for the Dedicated nodes? We can provision closer to your data residency controls.

Priya and I will draft two short runbooks after we get the answers: one for a Dedicated-only PoC and one for Private VPC (cost + access checklist). We'll include required IAM roles, peering steps, and test payloads.
